blocks.text: As Delhi's sovereign became slack in supervision, Gazdi grows swollen with pride and begins treating his ministerial authority as a stage for self-glorification. To fix that vanity in words, Gazdi asked Gang Bhat for praise and expected the bard to turn political power into poetic immortality.

Gang Bhat refuses to flatter what he does not believe, insisting that he would not eulogize what was not true. His refusal costs him his life, and the killing becomes a moral indictment of Gazdi's arrogance rather than a display of legitimate strength.

The page then broadens the accusation by suggesting that the same pride would damage Gazdi's larger alliances as well. What begins as a courtly demand for praise becomes an omen that Gazdi ruined the Marathas as well through the same blindness and overreach.
